Masonry for brick laid in lime

Lime mortar repointing for old Cincinnati brick

We rake out the old joint by hand, mix lime mortar to match your wall, pack it in layers and tool the profile to match.

Hard cement on soft brick breaks the brick

Brick laid before the 1930s was set in lime. The mortar has to stay softer than the brick, so the joint wears and the brick does not. Cement is harder than old brick: it traps water, and the face of the brick pops off instead.

That gray patch with crumbled brick around it? That is what we put right.

The sequence

Four stages, one joint

Pick a stage, or scroll on a wide screen, and watch one joint go from raked out to finished.

01 Rake out

A hand tool takes the old mortar back to twice the joint width, without nicking the brick.

Every job on old masonry, done soft-first

From one loose chimney course to a whole facade. Each job starts with a mortar match beside your wall.

  1. Lime mortar repointing

    Old joints raked out by hand and refilled with lime mortar softer than your old brick.

    Price it

  2. Chimney rebuild

    Loose chimney tops taken down to sound brick and relaid course by course to match.

    Price it

  3. Chimney crown

    A new sloped crown with a drip edge so water runs off instead of into the brick.

    Price it

  4. Brick replacement

    Spalled and cracked bricks cut out and replaced with salvaged brick close in size and color.

    Price it

  5. Limestone foundation repair

    Old limestone foundations repointed and loose stones reset, common under Cincinnati houses before 1920.

    Price it

  6. Hillside retaining walls

    Stone and block walls rebuilt on the slopes, with drainage behind them so they stay put.

    Price it

  7. Front stoops & steps

    Sagging brick and stone stoops taken apart, given a solid base and laid back level.

    Price it

  8. Mortar matching

    Test panels of sand, lime and tint made beside your wall until the new joint disappears.

    Price it

  9. Paint removal from brick

    Old paint taken off brick with low-pressure methods that leave the brick face intact.

    Price it

Two-year mortar promise

If new mortar cracks or comes loose within two years, we come back and repoint it at no charge.

Owen F. has repointed Cincinnati brick for 21 years

Italianates on the flats, rowhouses on the hills, limestone foundations under both. Each street has its own brick and its own mortar, and we have repointed enough of them to know which mixes hold.

We work across Cincinnati and in Covington, Newport, Norwood, Fort Thomas, Bellevue, Wyoming and Madeira.
